title: OAGRC structured deficiency register
description: Machine-readable metadata for corpus/deficiencies.md. The MARKDOWN IS CANONICAL; this artifact is annotation over it and never replaces it. It exists because the register's own summaries drifted -- three artifacts of this repository stated three different counts of its own defects (21, 24, 28) at the same moment -- and because a public register view built by regexing prose would be D-25 exactly: a reproducible coder mistaken for a correct one. Every field here is a HUMAN OR MODEL JUDGEMENT recorded explicitly, not a value inferred from the prose by a rule.

vocabulary_note.description: Why the vocabulary is shaped as it is. Required so the reasoning is not lost.

title.description: Copied from the markdown heading. Checked for exact equality by tools/check_register.py.

section_sha256.description: SHA-256 of this entry's markdown section. If the prose changes, this stops matching and the build fails, which FORCES RE-REVIEW rather than letting metadata quietly describe text it no longer matches. It does not establish that the judgements below were ever correct -- only that they were made against exactly this text.

finding_state.description: The status of the FINDING, kept separate from the status of any remediation. A finding can be active while fully remediated, and remediated while the historical damage is permanent.

evidence_class.description: How well the claimed origin is supported. This project cannot observe who first PRIVATELY noticed a defect, so it records where a defect was first substantively ARTICULATED IN PRESERVED MATERIAL, and how strong that evidence is.

investigation_triggered_by.description: A question or request that PROMPTED the work, which is not the same as the finding. The operator asking 'why 0.7?' triggered D-26 and D-28; the first preserved substantive articulation in both cases was the annotator's. Collapsing the two would inflate or deflate the project's central credibility statistic.

narrowed_or_corrected_by.description: Later parties who narrowed, corrected or reframed the entry. Recorded because 'who found it' and 'who fixed the overstatement in it' are different contributions and the register makes both.

affected_objects.description: ONE ROW PER AFFECTED OBJECT, because repairability is not a property of a deficiency. D-09 is the proof: the raw transcript's merged identities are not repairable, while the segments.json annotation was corrected. A single yes/no is false for one of them whichever way it is written.

prospective_control.description: Whether a forward requirement exists to stop recurrence, and whether it has been VALIDATED as opposed to merely written down. D-29's lesson: a check that is available is not a check that runs.

invalidates.description: Specific claims, predictions or artifacts this deficiency voids or weakens.

human_review.description: THE HONEST LIMIT OF THIS ARTIFACT. No deterministic check can establish that the metadata above agrees with the prose it describes; that is a semantic judgement. The build verifies structure, coverage, vocabulary and the section hash -- never meaning. This field records whether a human has actually read the entry against its metadata, and 'not_reviewed' is the truthful default rather than an omission.
